\chapter{Boolean Analysis — KKL}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.KKL
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This chapter develops the Fourier-analytic machinery behind the Kahn--Kalai--Linial
theorem and Friedgut's junta theorem: noisy influences
$\mathrm{Inf}_i^\rho[f] = \sum_{S \ni i}\rho^{\abs{S}-1}\hat f(S)^2$, the low- and
high-degree truncations of a Boolean function, the set of $\tau$-influential
coordinates, and the squared $L^2$ distance between Boolean functions.
On top of these it records the low-degree approximation bound
$\E[(f - f_{\le k})^2] \le I[f]/k$, the junta construction on the influential
coordinates, the KKL lower bound $\max_i \mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \ge \log n/(30n)$ for
balanced $\pm 1$-valued functions, and Friedgut's junta theorem.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Noisy influence]
\lean{KKL.noisyInfluence}
\statementsource{boolean-ch08-generalized-domains}{pdf-50833afe7403-p009-b003}
\label{KKL.noisyInfluence}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p009-b004,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p018-b003,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p023-b001
}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff}
The \emph{noisy influence} of coordinate $i$ on $f$ at noise rate $\rho$ is
\[
  \mathrm{Inf}_i^{\rho}[f] \;=\; \sum_{S \ni i} \rho^{\abs{S}-1}\,\hat f(S)^2,
\]
the sum being taken over all $S \subseteq [n]$ containing $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Low-degree truncation]
\lean{KKL.lowDegreePart}
\statementsource{boolean-ch08-generalized-domains}{pdf-50833afe7403-p014-b001}
\label{KKL.lowDegreePart}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff}
The \emph{low-degree part} of $f$ at level $k$ keeps only the Fourier coefficients
of degree at most $k$:
\[
  f_{\le k}(x) \;=\; \sum_{\abs{S}\le k} \hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[High-degree part]
\lean{KKL.highDegreePart}
\label{KKL.highDegreePart}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff}
The \emph{high-degree part} of $f$ at level $k$ keeps only the Fourier coefficients
of degree strictly greater than $k$:
\[
  f_{>k}(x) \;=\; \sum_{\abs{S} > k} \hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Influential coordinates]
\lean{KKL.influentialCoords}
\label{KKL.influentialCoords}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p022-b003}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence}
The set of $\tau$-\emph{influential} coordinates of $f$ is the finite set
\[
  J_\tau(f) \;=\; \{\, i \in [n] : \mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \ge \tau \,\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Junta]
\lean{KKL.IsJunta}
\label{KKL.IsJunta}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc}
A function $g$ is a \emph{$J$-junta} if it depends only on the coordinates in $J$:
whenever $x$ and $y$ agree on every $i \in J$, we have $g(x) = g(y)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Squared $L^2$ distance]
\lean{KKL.l2DistSq}
\label{KKL.l2DistSq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
The squared $L^2$ distance between two Boolean functions is
$\E\big[(f(x) - g(x))^2\big]$ under the uniform measure on the cube.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Noisy influence at noise rate one]
\lean{KKL.noisyInfluence_one}
\label{KKL.noisyInfluence_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_eq_sum_fourier, KKL.noisyInfluence}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a coordinate $i \in [n]$ and a Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$. At noise rate
$\rho = 1$, the noisy influence of $i$ on $f$ coincides with the ordinary influence of
$i$ on $f$:
\[
  \mathrm{Inf}_i^{1}[f] \;=\; \mathrm{Inf}_i[f].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Sum of noisy influences]
\lean{KKL.sum_noisyInfluence}
\label{KKL.sum_noisyInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, KKL.noisyInfluence}
\difficulty{3}
Fix an integer $n$ and a real number $\rho$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean
function. Summing the noisy influence at noise rate $\rho$ over all coordinates
$i\in[n]$ gives
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^{n} \mathrm{Inf}_i^{\rho}[f]
  \;=\; \sum_{S\subseteq[n]} \abs{S}\,\rho^{\,\abs{S}-1}\,\hat f(S)^2,
\]
where the right-hand sum ranges over all subsets $S$ of $[n]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Total influence as the sum of coordinate influences]
\lean{KKL.totalInfluence_eq_sum_influences}
\label{KKL.totalInfluence_eq_sum_influences}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function, and for each coordinate $i \in
\{1,\dots,n\}$ let $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \E\!\left[(f(x)-f(x^i))^2/4\right]$ denote the
influence of coordinate $i$, where $x^i$ is $x$ with its $i$-th bit flipped and $\E$ is
expectation under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. Then the total influence of $f$ is
the sum of the individual coordinate influences,
\[
  I[f] \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{n} \mathrm{Inf}_i[f].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Second moment of a $\pm 1$-valued function]
\lean{KKL.expect_sq_pm_one}
\label{KKL.expect_sq_pm_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct_self_pm_one, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a $\pm 1$-valued function, so that $f(x) \in \{-1, 1\}$
for every $x \in \{0,1\}^n$. Then, with respect to the uniform measure, $\E[f^2] = 1$;
that is, $2^{-n}\sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n} f(x)^2 = 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Parseval's identity for Boolean functions]
\lean{KKL.sum_fourier_sq_eq_expect_sq}
\label{KKL.sum_fourier_sq_eq_expect_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.parseval}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function. Then the sum of the squared
Fourier--Walsh coefficients of $f$ over all subsets $S \subseteq [n]$ equals the
expectation of $f^2$ under the uniform measure:
\[
  \sum_{S \subseteq [n]} \hat f(S)^2 \;=\; \E\!\left[f^2\right].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Low and high degree parts reconstruct the function]
\lean{KKL.low_plus_high_eq}
\label{KKL.low_plus_high_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion, KKL.highDegreePart, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function and let $k \in \bbn$ be a threshold
level. Then for every point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ of the cube,
\[
  f_{\le k}(x) + f_{>k}(x) = f(x),
\]
where $f_{\le k}(x) = \sum_{\abs{S}\le k}\hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x)$ and $f_{>k}(x) =
\sum_{\abs{S} > k}\hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x)$ are the low- and high-degree parts of $f$ at
level $k$. That is, splitting the Fourier–Walsh expansion of $f$ into frequencies of
degree at most $k$ and degree greater than $k$ recovers $f$ exactly.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier coefficients of the low-degree truncation]
\lean{KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart}
\label{KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.fourier_coeff_chi, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function and $k$ a natural number. For every
subset $S\subseteq[n]$, the Fourier--Walsh coefficient of the low-degree part $f_{\le
k}$ at frequency $S$ satisfies
\[
  \widehat{f_{\le k}}(S) \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    \hat f(S) & \text{if } \abs{S}\le k,\\[2pt]
    0 & \text{if } \abs{S} > k.
  \end{cases}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[$L^2$ error of the low-degree truncation]
\lean{KKL.lowDegree_l2_error}
\label{KKL.lowDegree_l2_error}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.parseval, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight, KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart, KKL.highDegreePart, KKL.l2DistSq, KKL.lowDegreePart, KKL.low_plus_high_eq}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function, and for a natural number $k$ let
$f_{\le k}(x) = \sum_{\abs{S}\le k} \hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x)$ be its low-degree part,
retaining only the Fourier--Walsh coefficients of degree at most $k$. Then, under the
uniform measure on the cube, the squared $L^2$ distance between $f$ and this truncation
equals the total Fourier weight sitting above level $k$:
\[
  \E\big[(f(x) - f_{\le k}(x))^2\big] \;=\; \sum_{\abs{S} > k} \hat f(S)^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function, and let $k$ be a positive integer.
Then the total Fourier weight of $f$ carried by frequencies of size strictly greater
than $k$ is bounded by the total influence divided by $k$:
\[
  \sum_{\substack{S \subseteq [n] \\ \abs{S} > k}} \hat f(S)^2 \;\le\; \frac{I[f]}{k}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, KKL.l2DistSq, KKL.lowDegreePart, KKL.lowDegree_l2_error, KKL.tail_fourier_weight_bound}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function and let $k\ge 1$ be an integer.
Writing $f_{\le k}(x)=\sum_{\abs S\le k}\hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x)$ for the truncation of $f$
to its Fourier coefficients of degree at most $k$, the squared $L^2$ distance between
$f$ and $f_{\le k}$ under the uniform measure on the cube is bounded by
\[
  \E\big[(f(x)-f_{\le k}(x))^2\big]\;\le\;\frac{I[f]}{k},
\]
where $I[f]=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$ is the total influence of $f$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Few influential coordinates]
\lean{KKL.influential_coords_card}
\label{KKL.influential_coords_card}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_eq_sum_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, KKL.influentialCoords}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function and let $\tau > 0$. The number of
$\tau$-influential coordinates of $f$ — those $i \in [n]$ with $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \ge
\tau$ — is bounded by
\[
  \abs{J_\tau(f)} \;\le\; \frac{I[f]}{\tau},
\]
where $I[f] = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$ is the total influence.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Low-degree part is close to a junta on the influential coordinates]
\lean{KKL.lowDegreePart_depends_on_influential}
\label{KKL.lowDegreePart_depends_on_influential}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.fourier_coeff_chi, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_eq_sum_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.parseval, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight, KKL.IsJunta, KKL.influentialCoords, KKL.l2DistSq, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{7}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function, let $k$ be a natural number, and let
$\tau>0$. Then there is a Boolean function $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ that is a junta on the
set $J_\tau(f)=\{\,i\in[n]:\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\ge\tau\,\}$ of $\tau$-influential
coordinates and that approximates the low-degree part $f_{\le k}$ in squared $L^2$
distance, namely
\[
  \E\big[(f_{\le k}(x)-g(x))^2\big]\;\le\;n\,\tau,
\]
where the expectation is taken under the uniform measure on the cube.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noisy influence is dominated by influence]
\lean{KKL.noisyInfluence_le_influence}
\label{KKL.noisyInfluence_le_influence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_eq_sum_fourier, KKL.noisyInfluence}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function, let $i\in[n]$ be a coordinate, and let
$\rho\in\bbr$ satisfy $0\le\rho\le 1$. Then the noisy influence of $i$ on $f$ at noise
rate $\rho$ is at most the influence of $i$ on $f$:
\[
  \mathrm{Inf}_i^{\rho}[f]\;\le\;\mathrm{Inf}_i[f].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noisy influence bounded by influence]
\lean{KKL.noisyInfluence_power_bound}
\label{KKL.noisyInfluence_power_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne, KKL.noisyInfluence, KKL.noisyInfluence_le_influence}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a $\pm 1$-valued Boolean function, let $i\in[n]$ be a
coordinate, and let $\rho$ be a noise rate with $0<\rho\le 1$. Then the noisy influence
of $i$ on $f$ at rate $\rho$ is at most the ordinary influence of $i$ on $f$:
\[
\mathrm{Inf}_i^{\rho}[f]\;=\;\sum_{S\ni i}\rho^{\abs{S}-1}\,\hat
f(S)^2\;\le\;\mathrm{Inf}_i[f].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cauchy–Schwarz bound on total influence]
\lean{KKL.cauchy_schwarz_influences}
\label{KKL.cauchy_schwarz_influences}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{2}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function, with
influences $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$ for $i = 1, \dots, n$ and total influence $I[f] =
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$. Then
\[
  I[f]^2 \;\le\; n \sum_{i=1}^{n} \mathrm{Inf}_i[f]^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Maximum influence bounds the normalized sum of squares]
\lean{KKL.max_influence_from_sum_sq}
\label{KKL.max_influence_from_sum_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_eq_sum_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function with positive total influence, $I[f]
= \sum_{j=1}^{n} \mathrm{Inf}_j[f] > 0$. Then some coordinate $i$ satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \;\ge\; \frac{\sum_{j=1}^{n} \mathrm{Inf}_j[f]^2}{I[f]}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Averaging bound for coordinate influence]
\lean{KKL.KKL_trivial}
\label{KKL.KKL_trivial}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.max_influence_lower_bound, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function. Then some
coordinate carries at least the average influence: there exists an index $i \in
\{1,\dots,n\}$ with
\[
  \mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \;\ge\; \frac{I[f]}{n},
\]
where $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$ is the influence of coordinate $i$ and $I[f] = \sum_{j=1}^n
\mathrm{Inf}_j[f]$ is the total influence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Noisy total influence]
\lean{KKL.noisyTotalInfluence}
\label{KKL.noisyTotalInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff}
The \emph{noisy total influence} at rate $\rho$ is
\[
  \sum_{S \subseteq [n]} \abs{S}\,\rho^{2\abs{S}}\,\hat f(S)^2 .
\]
\end{definition}

\lean{KKL.KKL_balanced}

  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p021-b002,

}
\label{KKL.KKL_balanced}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p012-b002,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p012-b003
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{

  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p021-b001,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p021-b002,

  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p022-b001,

}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff_empty, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne, BooleanAnalysis.max_influence_lower_bound, BooleanAnalysis.parseval_pm_one, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg, KKL.noisyInfluence, KKL.noisyInfluence_le_influence, KKL.sum_noisyInfluence}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$ be a $\pm 1$-valued Boolean function that is balanced,
meaning $\E[f] = 0$, and suppose $n \ge 2$. Then there is a coordinate $i \in [n]$ whose
influence satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \;\ge\; \frac{\log n}{30\,n}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Friedgut's junta theorem]
\lean{KKL.friedgut_junta}
\label{KKL.friedgut_junta}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{pdf-9d1751394783-p013-b001}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p023-b003,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p022-b003,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p022-b004,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p023-b001
}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight, KKL.IsJunta, KKL.influentialCoords, KKL.influential_coords_card, KKL.l2DistSq, KKL.lowDegreePart, KKL.lowDegreePart_depends_on_influential, KKL.lowDegree_approx}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$ be a $\pm 1$-valued Boolean function with total
influence $I[f]$, and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Then there exist a coordinate set $J
\subseteq [n]$ and a Boolean function $g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ such that
\[
  \abs{J} \;\le\; \frac{4n\,I[f]}{\varepsilon},
\]
$g$ is a $J$-junta, and $\E\big[(f(x) - g(x))^2\big] \le \varepsilon$ under the uniform
measure on the cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Balanced Boolean functions have total influence at least one]
\lean{KKL.balanced_totalInfluence_ge_one}
\label{KKL.balanced_totalInfluence_ge_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff_empty, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne, BooleanAnalysis.parseval_pm_one, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a $\pm 1$-valued Boolean function that
is balanced, meaning $\E[f] = 0$ under the uniform measure. Then its total influence
satisfies $I[f] \ge 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of the influence entropy]
\lean{KKL.influence_entropy_nonneg}
\label{KKL.influence_entropy_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_eq_sum_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function whose total influence $I[f] =
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$ is strictly positive. Then
\[
  0 \;\le\; \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]}{I[f]}\,
    \log\!\left(\frac{I[f]}{\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]}\right),
\]
where $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm.
\end{lemma}
